title: One night a year he checks your boots
idea: Krampus myth (heart-video recipe): the Krampus and Saint Nick check the boots door by door down an Alpine lane; Chip polishes his boot, hides in the woodpile, and finally swaps the drawings on the boots, so Spud's boot gets the birch sticks.

captions.text: In *Austria,* one night a year, *Krampus* checks every kid's boot.
ONE NIGHT A YEAR HE CHECKS YOUR BOOTS
I was gonna be good tomorr-
That's number nine. We're number four.
Saint Nick reads your whole year from the golden book. Good kids get chocolate.
My boot is *dirty.* Is that bad?!
Kids clean their boots for him. That's the rule.
Oh. He doesn't check the boot. He checks the *book.*
The bells aren't decoration. They're so you hear him coming.
This is just a story, right?
Every December they still walk the Alps. Hundreds of them.

visible.why: a snowy Alpine village at night, lit windows, a lane of wooden houses running up the hill
the Krampus' face: carved wood, curled horns, glowing eyes, a long red tongue
a small red boot on a snowy doorstep; a huge horned shadow falls over it
Saint Nick reads a glowing golden book and shakes his head; the horned Krampus holds a small kid up by the scruff
the kid dangles from his claw, pleading; the Krampus stuffs him over his shoulder into the wicker basket and slams the lid
down a snowy Alpine lane at night: two little potatoes peek out of their door, two boots with drawings pinned on their step
the old bishop turns a page of the glowing golden book
the Krampus: carved wooden face, curled horns, he bares his fangs, birch sticks in his fist
his wicker basket: the lid lifts, the kid peeks out, the lid slams shut on him
the little one holds up his muddy yellow felt boot in horror
he holds up the yellow boot, polished to a mirror shine, grinning
next door: a gleaming clean leather boot; Saint Nick shakes his head; the Krampus jams sticks into it anyway
he dives head first into the woodpile and pulls his feet in
up the lane the Krampus stops in the falling snow, sniffs the air like a dog and turns toward the woodpile
a grey tabby cat bolts out past his hooves; he turns to watch it go
the Krampus is right next door, bells swinging, snow sliding off the roof above the two little ones
a real Alpine Krampus run at night: dozens of horned, furry runners with torches and cowbells parade through a snowy square past potato onlookers
close: his hands swap the two crayon drawings between the teal boot and the yellow boot
Saint Nick kneels at the yellow boot (it now wears the teal drawing), reads a short glowing page and smiles
chocolate coins, mandarins and walnuts pour into the yellow boot; the little one beams
at the teal boot the page goes on and on: a long roll of fries pictures runs across the snow; he shakes his head
the Krampus jams birch sticks into the teal boot and turns to the tall one; his basket lid creaks open toward him
